title: Principles v2 against the core loops proposal
approval: Comparison read: principles v2 vs core loops

short.lead: The proposal is strong where v2 is about the long game: true forms with one rule each, events with their own warnings, loot that misbehaves, and data-driven systems. It is weakest where v2 is about the hook. Nothing in the proposal designs the first five minutes or the 15-second clip, the first reward lands about 12 to 15 minutes in, and the castle only hears your spells, not your talk, unless a player opts in. Your hook works as a pitch, but it holds three twists, and v2 says a 15-second clip can carry one.
short.hint: Tap a card for the detail. Suggested amendments to the proposal are under Changes, and seven of them are choices for you.

items: check
Agree
Where the two documents agree
done

One rule per monster (D12): every true form has one sense, one attack, one tell and one counter, the pattern of the Wick. The Visor is v2's Coil-Head rule and needs one player watching while the others move.
Warning signs (D13): every event has a far sign, its own sound, a clock in the world and a counter, which is v2's rule taken further.
The target misbehaves (D07): platinum cracks, flammable pieces catch fire, cursed pieces get heavier, mutter or summon your Echo.
Systems over content (D18, D21): variants, events, curses, quests and cycles are data assets that combine, which is your 'less with more' rule.
A run has a shape (D19): the portal clock, the Ophan's demand and the vault seals' greed choice give a goal, rising pressure and a moment to leave.
One new toy at a time (D20): phase 1 builds one true form per Age, and Market stock arrives in order.
Nothing from you.
stop
Disagree
Where they pull against each other
you

Fun by minute one (D04): v2 wants a first laugh in minute one and a first reward by minute five. The proposal's first raid is the normal 12 to 15 minutes, so the first sale comes after that. A new save also knows only Porta (fear pass, 2026-10-11), the escape spell the pitch says you cast 'exactly once, and too late', so the first spell a new player can say is not a fun one.

Cut fast (D22): v2 says build the smallest playable version and playtest within days. The proposal builds seven events, sixteen true forms, blackjack, cosmetics and a mod loader across nine weeks, with the only tuning pass in phase 3. The pitch's own riskiest question, whether shouting spells feels like power or embarrassment, is still untested: voice.md says no real voice has tried Velox or Saltus, and the haggle words were never tried with a real microphone.

Worth on screen (D03, D10): v2 says show the value at risk in the raid, like R.E.P.O.'s cart, so a viewer sees money being lost. The proposal's suggested answer to its own choice 1 keeps numbers out of the raid.
Your call on choices 4, 5 and 7.
search
Proposal misses
What v2 covers and the proposal does not
No clip design (D03). No list of the moments the game should produce, and voice casting fails v2's sound-off test unless the spoken word can be seen.
No style reward (D08), such as a bonus for a whispered Somnus or a raid that never raised the alarm.

Voice as a mechanic (D15): no decision on proximity voice chat or a walkie-talkie. Guards hearing ordinary talk is opt-in and off by default (voice.md, 'Chatter'). Only one of sixteen true forms, the Hush, listens for speech.
What the dead do (D17): a dead wizard can be carried out, but nothing gives them a role for the rest of a 12 to 15 minute raid.
A place to look things up (D05): v2 copies Lethal Company's bestiary; the ledger could hold one, but the proposal does not say so.
Tells you can see as well as hear (D13): ten of the sixteen true-form tells are sound only, for example the Visor's scrape, the Hush's breathing and the Fuse's hiss.
Solo play (D16), polish priorities (D23) and posting clips while building (D24) are not mentioned.
Nothing from you; the amendments are under Changes.
file
v2 misses
What the proposal covers and v2 does not

Speech as the controls. None of v2's three games casts by voice, so v2 says nothing about misheard words as comedy, recognition speed, loudness as a choice, or the embarrassment risk. This is PlunderSpell's main twist and needs its own principle.
A boss you serve and finally beat. v2's long loop stops at quotas and island bosses; it has no principle for a campaign arc or an ending.
Luck may gate only optional progress. Your rule that required progress never depends on luck has no v2 principle.
Your actions set off events. v2's D18 comes close, but 'every act has a clear consequence' is not stated.
The economy and gambling: prices, a shop where each item counters a named threat, and blackjack. v2 mentions a casino only as optional depth.
Voice privacy, mods, and cosmetics as progression.
Nothing from you. These could become D25 onwards in v2 later.
eye
15 seconds
The 15-second viewer hook
you
v2's checklist: seconds 0 to 3 show gameplay, seconds 3 to 8 the familiar frame, seconds 8 to 15 the twist and something going wrong, and it must read with the sound off.
Your hook has three twists: a castle that listens, spells you speak, and an enemy you serve. v2's D02 says pick one; the others come later.

'The castle listens' and 'voice spells' are really one twist: your voice is both your power and your danger. That fits 15 seconds. 'An enemy you serve' is the hours hook and belongs in a longer trailer and the Steam page.

A clip the proposal already makes possible: three wizards creep down a torchlit corridor carrying a gold chalice (the familiar frame); one shouts IGNIS at a guard, the book under their arm catches fire, the guard turns into its true form, and they run, dropping the chalice.
Sound-off fails today: the HUD caption shows what the recogniser heard ('igneous -> IGNIS'), which is a debug line, not something a viewer reads at a glance.
Your call on choice 1, the 15-second line.
flask
5 minutes
The 5-minute player hook
you

Minute 0 to 1, 'do something with a borrowed skill': partly met. Picking up and carrying loot is borrowed from physics games, and talking is borrowed from every co-op game. Speaking a fun spell is not possible, because a new save knows only Porta.
Minute 1, first laugh: likely, through misfires and physics, but the proposal does not plan it.
Minutes 1 to 3, the first goal shown clearly: the ledger shows the Ophan's demand, but that demand falls due only every 3 to 5 raids.
Minutes 3 to 5, first success and reward: not met. The first sale comes after a full raid.
By minute 5, a hint of danger and depth: met. Guards are visible from the gate (fear pass), and the dial plaque previews the next Age.

'Don't return home empty-handed': in the proposal, coming home empty costs only coin. Empty hands are fatal in the castle, when the Ophan arrives. The line is true in spirit; the tightest wording is 'don't be empty-handed when it comes'.
Your call on choices 2 and 4: the first spell and the first raid.
hand
Your calls
Seven choices that could feed the proposal
you
The proposal still waits on your approval, so any answer here can be folded into it before the four workstreams start.
Each choice under Choices has my suggestion marked.
Pick an answer for each of the seven choices, or say which to drop.

changes: new
A designed first session
A scripted-light opening that hits v2's five-minute checklist.

The proposal designs the loops, not the opening. Suggested: the company wakes in the Lair as the Ophan writes its first demand into the ledger; the first raid is short, with the demanded piece in the first rooms; the Ophan is seen arriving as the portal closes; the first sale at the Fence comes at about minute 6. Choice 4.
The first raid is a normal 12 to 15 minute raid.
A first raid built to teach the loop.
A new player meets the master, the danger and the reward in one sitting.
new
The spoken word made visible
The cast word appears in the world, so clips read with the sound off.

D03 asks for clips that work without sound. A shouted word could flash as carved letters in lapis, the colour your style reserves for the voice, louder words bigger. It replaces the debug-looking HUD caption in clips and fits the diegetic rule.
A HUD caption shows what the recogniser heard.
The word drawn in the world, sized by loudness.
A muted clip still shows what was said and why the wall fell.
new
A castle that listens to talk
Guards hear ordinary talk by default, with a keys-only path.

Your hook says the castle listens. Today it hears casts (a shout wakes the castle) but hears ordinary talk only if a player opts in. Suggested: on by default, with the off switch kept for players who cannot or will not speak, and one true form per Age that listens for speech. Choice 3.
Chatter is opt-in, off by default; one true form, the Hush, listens.
Listening on by default, one listener per Age.
Every whisper and every panicked shout matters, which is the hook.
new
A role for dead wizards
The dead stay in the raid.
D17: a dead player who waits ten minutes picks up their phone. Suggested: a ghost that can whisper to the living and that the household can also hear. Choice 6.
The dead are carried out or wait.
A ghost with a whisper.
Death becomes a story instead of a break.
new
A style bonus
Extra pay for the hard, showy way.
D08. Candidates: a whispered Somnus that lands, a raid with no alarm raised, platinum carried home without a crack. Paid at the counter as a named bonus.
Only the haul's worth is paid.
A bonus for style.
Skilled players get something to chase, and clips get a reason to exist.

A bestiary in the ledger
One place to look up a true form once met.
D05: the world teaches, but players need a place to check. Meeting a true form writes its tell and counter into the ledger book.
Nothing to look things up in.
Ledger pages per true form.
Fewer stuck players, and no wall of text up front.

A playtest gate after phase 1
Test the fun before building phase 2.
D22. Phase 1 ends with a four-player playtest, timed against v2's 15-second and 5-minute checklists, before blackjack, curses and the rest begin. Choice 7.
Tuning happens only in phase 3.
A playtest gate at week 3.
Bad ideas are cut before eight weeks of work stack on them.

A visible loss in the raid, without bringing back a HUD.
No numbers in the raid (proposal 1A)
Loss shown in the world, numbers in the Lair and Market

D10 says show the value at risk. Suggested middle path: a knock chips coins or sparks off the piece and its shine dims a step, and the pile in the portal glows brighter as it grows. Numbers stay in the Lair and Market. Choice 5.

D06: never show a system the player does not need yet. Action events, such as the vault seals, can stay from the start, because the player chooses them.

Every tell is seen and heard
D13 asks for two forms per warning, for deaf and hard-of-hearing players and for muted clips. For example, the Visor's plates could catch the light as it moves.

Kept as proposed; they already match v2.
The true-form table, the seven events with their own warnings, the loot variants and the data-asset approach all pass v2's tests on paper. They still need the playtests v2 describes.

wrapup.summary: A comparison of game design principles v2 with the PlunderSpell core loops proposal, and a test of your hook against v2's 15-second and 5-minute checklists.
